name: Highlight
purpose: Discover literal queries in plain text through exact Atom behavior and render finished semantic match styling.
useWhen: One plain text string needs deterministic visible query matches without recreating escaping, overlap, case, or whole-word behavior.

avoidWhen.condition: The relevant passage is already selected by the author.
Content is arbitrary React nodes or the application needs active result navigation.
avoidWhen.useInstead: application-owned rich-content traversal or search navigation

composition: Pass plain text through text and literal query values through query; keep surrounding sentence typography on Text or another content owner.
Let Highlight delegate all matching to Atom and keep search input, active result, counters, and navigation in the application.

rules.statement: Use exact Atom Highlight behavior; do not copy or replace its segmentation, escaping, overlap, or exact-match logic.
Use Highlight only for plain text and literal queries, never by flattening or cloning arbitrary React content.
Preserve Brick's fixed native span root and Atom-generated native mark matches.
Select only the documented subtle, solid, or underline variant and accent or neutral tone.
Keep search state, active-result navigation, counts, keyboard commands, and announcements outside Highlight.
Load styles.css or core.css plus highlight.css.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using Mark or a consumer regular expression to discover query matches.
commonMistakes.correction: Pass the plain string and literal query to Highlight so exact Atom behavior owns segmentation.

validation: Confirm literal, empty, repeated, overlapping, punctuation, Unicode, case-sensitive, whole-word, and first-match-only inputs preserve original text and copy order.
Confirm native span and mark output, closed recipes, forced colors, wrap, zoom, text spacing, localization, RTL, SSR, refs, and CSS delivery without focus or interaction.
